history.period: Ancient (origins are legendary; no archaeologically dated structure)
history.summary: The Bhagsunag Temple at Bhagsu village (~2 km from McLeod Ganj) is dedicated jointly to Lord Shiva and the serpent deity Bhagsunag. Local legend says King Bhagsu stole water from the sacred Nag Dal Lake, fought the Nag Devta, was defeated and forgiven, and the site was named Bhagsu(nag) for their reconciliation; the temple's sacred spring-fed kund is believed to have healing powers. Tourism blogs repeat a 5,000-5,100-year age claim - this is legend, not a documented date. The temple shows traditional Himachali architecture with a prominent white shikhara, is deeply revered by the local Gorkha community, and is the trailhead for the Bhagsu waterfall walk. FLAG: CSV town 'Dharamshala' is approximate; the temple is in Bhagsu village near McLeod Ganj (Upper Dharamshala).

name: Bhagsunag Temple
town_description: Bhagsu is a village about 2 km northeast of McLeod Ganj, the upper suburb of Dharamshala in Kangra district, at the foot of the Dhauladhar range; it is a busy stop on the Bhagsu waterfall and Triund trek routes.

travel.airport: Kangra Airport (Gaggal, DHM), about 15 km from McLeod Ganj; taxis readily available.
travel.railway: Pathankot Junction, about 85-90 km, is the nearest major railhead; the narrow-gauge Kangra Valley Railway runs Pathankot to Jogindernagar.
travel.road: About 2-3 km from McLeod Ganj (walkable or short taxi/auto ride) and about 9 km from Dharamshala; the Bhagsu waterfall is a 15-30 minute walk behind the temple.

visitor_information.best_time: March to June and October to February for pleasant weather; the Bhagsu waterfall is at its fullest during the monsoon (July-September).
visitor_information.opening_hours: Reported as 5:00 AM-12:00 PM and 4:00-9:00 PM (Holidify); other sources list 5:00 AM-8:00 PM - verify before visiting. No entry fee.
